title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DR Congo a global health emergency
byline: The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s eastern Ituri province a public health emergency of international concern.

title: Low-pressure area located to the north weakening: Met. Department
byline: The low-pressure area located to the north of Sri Lanka is gradually weakening, the Department of Meteorology said today.

title: IMF to consider Sri Lanka’s fifth, sixth reviews on May 27
byline: The International Monetary Fund’s Executive Board is to review the fifth and sixth reviews of Sri Lanka’s Extended Fund Facility (EFF) programme on May 27, 2026.

title: Minister orders action over hospital medicine shortages
byline: Concerns over medicine shortages, equipment limitations and administrative inefficiencies at the Colombo National Hospital (CNH) came under sharp focus during a high-level management meeting held at the hospital recently, prompting the Deputy Health Minister to order an urgent review of supply and service systems.

title: Two nabbed in Hatton over Rs. 4 million Telecom cable theft racket
byline: Two suspects have been arrested by officers of the Hatton Police Criminal Investigation Division for allegedly cutting, burning, and stealing telephone cables belonging to the Hatton Telecom office in the Norwood, Maskeliya and Castlereagh areas.

title: Rs. 50 million plasma exchange machines donated to Health Ministry
byline: The Health Ministry has received two advanced blood plasma exchange machines worth over Rs. 50 million, donated to strengthen treatment services for leptospirosis and blood-related cancer patients in Sri Lanka.

title: Wanawasala train crash: Stolen rail parts sold for Rs. 3,000
byline: The railway components dismantled from the site of the Wanawasala train accident were sold for a meager sum of Rs. 3,000, according to Deputy Inspector General (DIG) of Police for the Western Province North, Kalinga Jayasinghe. Speaking at a press conference today (17), the DIG revealed that th police have identified the location where the stolen parts were purchased and have taken the establishment’s owner into custody.

title: EC calls for updates to 2026 voter register via GN officers
byline: The Election Commission has urged individuals who have not been included in the 2026 electoral register, or those who have changes in their address, name, or National Identity Card (NIC) details, as well as those born before 01 February 2009, to contact their respective Grama Niladhari officers for verification and updates.

title: Rescue diver dies during search for bodies of Italians who drowned in Maldives caves
byline: A rescue diver has died while searching for the bodies of a group of Italians who died in a scuba-diving accident in the Maldives.

title: 8 balls in, Pathirana suffers injury blow
byline: Matheesha Pathirana’s long-awaited debut for Kolkata Knight Riders ended in disappointment after the Sri Lankan pacer suffered an injury just eight deliveries into the clash against Gujarat Titans.

title: Exchange rate error costs People’s Bank Rs. 656 Mn
byline: The People’s Bank said that it is in the process of recovering approximately Rs. 656 million mistakenly paid to customers following a systemic exchange rate error in its remittance platform that affected transactions processed between May 2023 and March 2026.

title: Bulgaria wins Eurovision Song Contest, Israel comes second again
byline: Bulgaria won the Eurovision Song Contest for the first time on Saturday in a final overshadowed ​by five countries’ boycott over Gaza, claiming a dramatic victory despite another big public vote for Israel that again secured it ‌second place.

title: 12 major reservoirs open spill gates, 6 at medium level
byline: The Irrigation Department says that the spill gates of 12 major reservoirs and 06 medium-sized reservoirs have been opened due to the prevailing rainy weather conditions.

title: Malwana student standoff draws PM’s attention
byline: The attention of the Education, Higher Education and Vocational Education Minister, and Prime Minister Dr. Harini Amarasuriya has been drawn to the situation involving a group of university students who have been staying for several days on a land in the Malwana area under the custody of the Dompe Divisional Secretariat.

title: WHO declares Ebola outbreak in DR Congo a global health emergency
byline: The World Health Organization (WHO) has declared an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s eastern Ituri province a public health emergency of international concern.

title: Colonial-era artefacts are more than museum pieces: Hemachandra
byline: Cultural objects displaced during the colonial period should not be viewed merely as museum possessions, but as part of the living heritage, identity, and historical memory of nations and peoples, Acting Foreign Minister Arun Hemachandra said while addressing the inauguration of the “Whose Law?” Research Conference held in Colombo on 13 May 2026.

title: Low-pressure system North of Sri Lanka weakens; Final weather bulletin issued
byline: The Meteorology Department says the low-pressure area located north of Sri Lanka has weakened, with its impact on the Bay of Bengal and surrounding sea areas gradually reducing.

title: Mental health safeguards urged in Keheliya drug case as trial nears end
byline: Calls are mounting for the implementation of formal mental health safeguards for suspects involved in the ongoing high-profile pharmaceutical-related case linked to former Health Minister Keheliya Rambukkella, as the lengthy trial approaches its final stage before the Colombo High Court.

title: Ukraine drones kill four in Russia, Moscow faces biggest attack in over a year
byline: At least four people were killed, including three in the Moscow region, after Ukraine launched its biggest overnight drone attack on the Russian capital in more ​than a year, local officials said on Sunday.

title: Hanif Yusoof clarifies Governor role amid speculation
byline: Western Province Governor Hanif Yusoof has clarified recent media speculation regarding his position, stating that he had earlier informed President Anura Kumara Dissanayake of his desire to step down from the post.

title: Two Nepali Sherpa climbers break own records on Mount Everest
byline: Two renowned Nepali guides have scaled Mount Everest with one called the “Everest Man” breaking his own record set last year with a 32nd climb and the other, known as the “Mountain Queen”, breaking her own women’s record with an 11th summit.

title: Scotland rugby great Scott Hastings dead at 61
byline: Scotland great Scott Hastings died at the age of 61 on Sunday after suffering from cancer, the Scottish Rugby Union announced Sunday.

title: Sri Lanka wins two Bronze medals
byline: Sri Lankan school boxers Amodhya Jayarathna and Himaya Hettiarachchi secured two bronze medals at the Asian Under-15 and Under-17 Boxing Championship 2026, held in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.

title: Victoria Reservoir drowning: three youths dead
byline: Three youths have drowned after an incident at the Victoria Reservoir in the Bambaragala Temple area in Teldeniya, police said.

title: Muslims in Sri Lanka to mark Eid on May 28
byline: Muslims in Sri Lanka will celebrate the Hajj festival (Eid al-Adha) on May 28, according to an announcement by the Colombo Grand Mosque.

title: Puvitharan sets new Sri Lankan pole vault record
byline: National athlete Arunthavarasa Puvitharan of the Sri Lanka Army Sports Club created a new Sri Lanka record in the men’s pole vault event.

title: Veteran journalist D.B.S. Jeyaraj passes away at 72
byline: D.B.S. Jeyaraj, one of Sri Lanka’s most respected veteran journalists and political commentators, has passed away in Canada at the age of 72.

title: Western Province Governor to step down after successor is appointed
byline: Western Province Governor Hanif Yusoof has resigned from his post and will officially step down once a suitable successor is appointed, according to a statement issued by him.
